limitations: This is a bytecode/string-reference scan and does not execute every game version or instrument arbitrary runtime-generated bytecode.
No custom launcher, Java agent, third-party mod set, or modified network pipeline was captured.
The component-level Netty SNI probe establishes vulnerable fallback behavior only when an SniHandler is actually constructed; it is not a Minecraft runtime exploit.
Minecraft owns the affected libraries; no compatible Mojang update or project-controlled dependency override was applied.

reachability_conclusion.confidence: High for the exact official unmodified game classpaths; insufficient to clear mixed-mod or custom-launcher deployments.
reachability_conclusion.official_unmodified_minecraft_client_and: No SniHandler caller or class-name reflection reference was found in the scanned Minecraft client binaries or default runtime library classpath. The stock game packet pipeline does not select SNI TLS; this CVE is not reached by the scanned vanilla client/integrated-server path.
reachability_conclusion.third_party_mods_custom_launchers_agents: Not scanned; a third-party mod or custom launcher can construct SniHandler or mutate the pipeline. Its libraries, reflective loaders, and runtime instrumentation are outside Mojang manifests.

runtime_classpath_scan.method: Scan every .class entry in each exact Minecraft client JAR and every default runtime libraries.artifact JAR from the pinned Mojang version metadata. Search constant-pool/classfile bytes for SniHandler binary names (including reflective class-name strings) and Netty SslHandler/SslContext references. Native classifiers are not Java classpath JARs and are excluded.

upstream_authority.precondition: Server-side SniHandler falls back to a weaker default SslContext when the TLS ClientHello handshake header is fragmented across TLS records; impact requires per-SNI clientAuth to be the only authentication gate.
